picks.analysis: Denver's defensive coordinator installed a two-high shell specifically designed to take away Tua's bread-and-butter timing routes — the slants and crossing patterns that operate in the 0-8 yard window. Camp footage shows the Broncos' nickel personnel running a disguised Cover-6 that collapses exactly where Tagovailoa's first read lands. Atlanta's WR corps hasn't seen this look in joint practices, and Tua's debut pressure in a new system creates exactly the kind of hesitation the Broncos are hunting. Getting the Broncos as a double-digit underdog in a game where they have the schematic edge is the sharpest number on the board this week.

With Kyler Murray named the starter, the Vikings are leaning on his experience to guide the offense. Reports from camp indicate that Murray has been sharp, benefiting from increased first-team reps. Meanwhile, the Giants are still working through QB competition dynamics, with Jaxson Dart needing to show more consistency. This gives the Vikings a clear edge, especially with their defensive rotations looking solid in practice.

The Bills have been showcasing a tight-knit offensive unit in camp, with Josh Allen looking particularly sharp. Carolina's camp has been marred by injuries, notably to Nic Scourton, which has impacted their linebacker rotations. Buffalo's offensive line has been cohesive, giving Allen the protection needed to exploit mismatches against a depleted Panthers defense.

Daniel Jones' impressive return from injury has been the highlight of Colts camp, with the QB showing no signs of his previous Achilles issues. The Patriots are still adjusting to new schemes under Mike Vrabel, with some inconsistency noted in their secondary. The Colts' offensive line has been dominant, providing Jones with ample time to connect with his receivers.

The 49ers are dealing with significant injuries, including the loss of Ricky Pearsall, which has disrupted their offensive plans. Tennessee, with a more stable roster and a solid showing in camp, has been able to focus on refining their schemes. The Titans' defensive line has been particularly impressive, ready to capitalize on San Francisco's weakened receiving corps.
